cases.headline: Tesla Model Y's Full Self-Driving Stops Dead at Green Light, Owner Forced To Accelerate Through Intersection
cases.source_summary: A Tesla Model Y owner is raising concerns about the company’s Full Self-Driving software after their brand-new SUV suddenly stopped in the middle of an intersection. The driver says the vehicle had a green left-turn…
cases.narrative: A Tesla Model Y owner posted a 15-second video and account saying the car, running Full Self-Driving version 14.3, stopped in an intersection during a left turn on a green signal after detecting a truck with yellow warning lights. The owner said nothing was directly behind and that the car stayed still until the accelerator was pressed. No collision is reported, and the report notes the account does not establish why the software stopped. The date and place are not given.

cases.headline: Woman arrested after self-driving Tesla crashes into construction equipment while she was allegedly intoxicated in western Indiana
cases.source_summary: A 57-year-old woman in Vigo County, Indiana, was arrested after her Tesla, operating in self-driving mode, crashed into construction equipment on Interstate 70. The driver was intoxicated, failed sobriety tests, and faces multiple charges.
cases.narrative: At about 10:30 p.m. on November 19, 2026, a 2016 Tesla struck two arrow boards in a construction zone on eastbound I-70 near mile marker 13 in Vigo County, Indiana. Indiana State Police said their investigation found the car was in self-driving mode; no product was named and one outlet describes the mode as alleged. No one was hurt, though workers were nearby. The driver, 57, was arrested after a test showed a blood alcohol content of 0.14% and was charged with three offences related to intoxicated driving and a highway work zone.

cases.headline: Tesla on autopilot crashed into 2 trucks in Somerset County while driver did her makeup
cases.source_summary: Montgomery Township police responded to the motor vehicle crash on Rt. 206 near Wood Thrush Lane at around 11:28 a.m. on Nov. 2, according to a statement from the department. A 37-year-old woman from ...
cases.narrative: At about 11:28 a.m. on November 2, 2026, a 2022 Tesla Model Y heading north on Route 206 in Montgomery Township, New Jersey, crossed the centre line and struck a tractor-trailer and then a garbage truck. Police said the car was being operated in Autopilot mode and the driver was applying makeup; one report says investigators concluded she probably grabbed the steering wheel while shifting in her seat, which stopped Autopilot. The two truck drivers had minor injuries and the Tesla driver was unhurt. Police issued the driver summonses for careless driving, reckless driving and failure to maintain lane.

cases.headline: Tesla confirms Autopilot or FSD activity during fatal crash in Florida — Electrek
cases.source_summary: Tesla's federal filing confirmed a driver-assistance system was engaged before a fatal Florida crash, but the narrative explaining what happened is redacted.
cases.narrative: At 11:43 p.m. on September 30, 2026, a 2025 Tesla Model X left Golden Gate Parkway near Estuary Boulevard in Naples, Florida, hit a traffic signal pole and rolled over. A 50-year-old passenger was killed and the 48-year-old driver had non-life-threatening injuries. The Florida Highway Patrol said the crash remains under investigation. Electrek reported in November that Tesla's own crash report to NHTSA lists the driver-assistance feature as verified engaged with a pre-crash speed of 39 mph, with the narrative redacted; coverage notes this is not a finding of cause.

cases.headline: A man whose Tesla crashed into a house last month in Texas and killed a woman while he was using its autopilot function has been charged with manslaughter, court records show.
cases.source_summary: After a Tesla crashed into a Katy home, killing a woman inside, officials said the driver claimed the vehicle was on autopilot when the crash happened. The driver was later arrested for the crash as records say his claim wasn't true.
cases.narrative: A Tesla Model 3 left the road in Katy, Texas, on a Friday night and struck a house, killing a 76-year-old woman. The driver told Harris County sheriff's deputies the car was on Autopilot. A Tesla vice president wrote that the driver had overridden the system by pressing the accelerator fully, and the NTSB's preliminary findings, as reported a month later, also said the driver overrode the driver-assistance system. NHTSA opened a special investigation, and the sheriff's office said it would present its findings to the district attorney.

cases.headline: Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3
cases.source_summary: Tesla confirms Autopilot or FSD was engaged at 71 mph when a Model 3 hit an overturned truck on I-75 in Naples, killing three. Nobody told the public.
cases.narrative: Just before 4 a.m. on May 31, 2026, a 2023 Tesla Model 3 struck an overturned box truck on southbound I-75 near Naples, Florida, and a man who had stopped to help the truck's driver. Two of the Tesla's passengers and the man who stopped were killed; the Tesla's driver and two other passengers were seriously hurt. A Florida Highway Patrol trooper said the driver would have seen only the truck's unlit underside. Electrek reported in November that Tesla's own crash report to NHTSA lists the driver-assistance feature as verified engaged with a pre-crash speed of 71 mph, with the narrative redacted.

cases.headline: Tesla settles a fatal Full Self-Driving crash lawsuit
cases.source_summary: A settlement is the sound a lawsuit makes when it stops. For Tesla, one just went quiet. The far louder problem, a federal safety investigation, is still talking. Tesla has settled a lawsuit tied to a ...
cases.narrative: In 2023 a Tesla Model Y struck and killed a 71-year-old woman who had got out of her car on an Arizona highway and was waving traffic around an earlier crash caused by sun glare. Coverage ties the crash to Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) system. Her daughter's lawsuit against Tesla was settled on undisclosed terms in June 2026. The crash is one of four that prompted an NHTSA investigation of the system in low visibility, which was escalated to an engineering analysis in March 2026.

cases.headline: Tesla Challenges $243 Million Florida Crash Verdict, Says Driver Ignored Autopilot Warnings
cases.source_summary: Tesla is asking a federal appeals court to overturn a $243 million judgment stemming from a fatal Florida Keys crash, arguing that a distracted driver, rather than defects in its Autopilot system, ...
cases.narrative: On April 25, 2019, a 2019 Tesla Model S with Autopilot engaged ran a stop sign at about 62 mph at a T-intersection on Card Sound Road near Key Largo, Florida, and struck a parked SUV, which hit two people standing nearby; one was killed and one seriously injured. The driver, who had looked down to retrieve a dropped phone, was cited for careless driving and pleaded no contest, with adjudication withheld. In August 2025 a federal jury found Tesla 33% responsible; Tesla's share of the judgment is about $243 million. Tesla filed an appeal brief on November 6, 2026, arguing the distracted driver caused the crash; the appeals court has not ruled.
